summary: David Brainerd Spooner was an Indologist and archaeologist who studied at Stanford University (~1895–1899). He served as Directeur p. i. of the Archaeological Survey of India (~1919–1925).

David Brick is an Indologist who studied under Patrick Olivelle. He served on the editorial board of Anthem South Asian Normative Traditions Studies in 2012 and as a professor at Yale University (attested 2012–2018).

David Brown was a scholar of Indology and religious studies who studied at Magdalene College, Cambridge (1782). He served as Provost of Fort William College (~1800–1807) and founded the Calcutta Auxiliary Bible Society.

David Bubna-Litic earned his PhD from Western Sydney University and worked in Buddhist studies and related fields. In 2000, he was attested as Lecturer in Strategic Management and Responsible Business at the University of Technology Sydney.

David Burton, a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, earned his doctorate at the University of Bristol (1994–1997). He was a Junior Research Fellow at Keble College, Oxford (attested 2001) and Senior Lecturer at Canterbury Christ Church University (attested 2010).

David Dean Shulman is an Indologist and religious studies scholar who studied at Hebrew University and the University of London under John Ralston Marr. His career was at Hebrew University as a professor, editor (~1976–2017), and director (1992–1998).

David Drewes is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology who earned degrees from Lawrence University, the University of Virginia (PhD 2006 under Karen Christina Lang), and studied at Wisconsin-Madison. He became Assistant Professor at the University of Manitoba (attested 2008–2010).

David E. Cooper is a philosopher who studied at Highgate School and St Edmund Hall. He was a lecturer at Oxford (1967), Professor of Philosophy at Durham University (1986–2008), and a Distinguished International Visiting Professor at Peking University (2022).

David E. Riggs, a specialist in Japanology and Buddhist studies, earned his Ph.D. from UCLA. He taught at UC Santa Barbara, UIUC, and UH Mānoa, and held posts at the International Research Center for Japanese Studies (2006) and Oberlin College (2010).

David Faure is a sinologist and historian who studied at the University of Hong Kong and Princeton University. He taught at Indiana University Bloomington, lectured at St Antony's College (1990), and directed at The Chinese University of Hong Kong (~2006).

David Fiordalis, a specialist in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology, studied at Carleton College, the University of Chicago, and the University of Michigan (PhD under Luis Oscar Gómez). In 2017, he was associate professor and chair at Linfield University.

David Friedman (1903–1984) worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. Between approximately 1950 and 1970, he held appointments as Reader in Indian Philosophy at SOAS and as Professor at the University of London.

David Gellner is a scholar of religious studies, Buddhist studies, and Indology. He has held appointments at the University of Oxford (attested 1988), serving as Emeritus Professor of Social Anthropology at Oxford and Wolfson College (attested 2026).

David Germano is a Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his PhD at the University of Wisconsin-Madison in 1992. He has served on the faculty at the University of Virginia, including as Associate Professor of Tibetan and Buddhist Studies (attested 2000–2008).
David Gonsalez is an expert in Tibetology and Buddhist studies who completed traditional studies under teachers Lobsang Choephel, Lati Rinpoche, Kirti Tsenshab Rinpoche, and Denma Lochö Rinpoche.

David Gordon White, an Indologist and religious studies scholar, studied at Wisconsin-Madison, Banaras Hindu University, the Sorbonne, and the University of Chicago (PhD ~1979–1988). He taught at the University of Virginia and the University of California, Santa Barbara.

David Higgins is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and philosophy. He has held positions as a researcher at the University of Vienna (attested 2015) and as a Research Fellow at the International Institute for Buddhist Studies (attested 2026).

David J. Kalupahana was a Buddhist studies and philosophy scholar who studied at the University of Ceylon and SOAS, University of London. He was an assistant lecturer at Ceylon (~1959–1972) and Department of Philosophy Chairman at UH Mānoa (1972).

David Jones, a scholar of philosophy and religious studies, received his Ph.D. from the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa. He served as a philosophy professor in the University System of Georgia and director of the Center for the Development of Asian Studies (attested 2007).

David K. Wyatt was a historian who studied at Harvard, Boston University, and Cornell University. He taught at SOAS (~1966–1968), Michigan (~1968–1969), and served as history department chair at Cornell (1969–2002) and president of the Association for Asian Studies (1993).
